# India intensifies talks with Russia, Ukraine to end war

## New Delhi is discussing with Moscow and Kiev the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, grain exports and energy.

![India intensifies talks with Russia, Ukraine to end war](https://cdn4.focus.bg/fakti/photos/medium/742/india-aktivira-razgovorite-s-rusia-i-ukraina-za-krai-na-voinata-1.webp)

India has stepped up its contacts with Russia and Ukraine in an attempt to help end the war, External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar said at the Munich Security Conference leaders' meeting in New Delhi.

“In recent months, we have become a little more engaged beyond advocacy and are talking to both Russia and Ukraine,“ Jaishankar said. According to him, India is trying to be helpful on specific issues related to the conflict.

## Discussing shipping, grain and energy

Among the topics are the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, the export of grain and energy resources, as well as options for preventing mutual attacks. The Indian minister did not specify whether the talks led to a specific agreement or an agreed timetable for negotiations.

For years, India has been calling on Moscow and Kiev to seek a solution through diplomacy. “We want to see an end to this conflict and we believe that dialogue and diplomacy are needed for this“, Jaishankar said. He stressed that negotiations are a necessary part of the process.

# Open Architecture, Closed Borders: Inside the RISC-V Exception to US-China Tech Decoupling

While export controls tighten on advanced chips, American and Chinese engineers are deepening collaboration on the instruction set architecture that may shape computing's next decade.

MH

Marcus Halloran

Developer Tools Reporter· Singapore

Oct 5, 2026

6min read

Credit: Handout

## A Rare Island of Cooperation

At Opentechwire, we've tracked semiconductor export controls as they've tightened month by month since 2022. GPU thresholds drop, lithography tools disappear from shipping manifests, and design software licences vanish. Yet one corner of chip development remains conspicuously open: RISC-V, the instruction set architecture that defines how processors decode commands. MIPS, the intellectual property provider acquired by GlobalFoundries in 2025, is now collaborating with Chinese firms "very closely" on RISC-V standardisation, according to chief technology officer Yankin Tanurhan. The partnership underscores a paradox that few policymakers have resolved - how to contain advanced chip capabilities whilst an open-source blueprint for processor design flows freely across borders.

RISC-V is not a physical chip. It is a specification, a shared language that tells silicon how to execute instructions. Because the architecture is open-source and maintained by a Switzerland-base
